failures.title: Lexus 2UR-GSE Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Coolant valley plate leak - all 2UR-GSE models
items.whatHappens: The 2UR‑GSE uses a valley plate seal between the V of the engine block. Over time, the sealant can fail, allowing coolant to seep from the valley. This is a slow, progressive leak - owners report topping up the coolant reservoir every few months initially, with the leak worsening over time. A faint coolant smell is often the first warning sign. The issue appears to affect newer RC F and GS F models as well as older IS F units. UK owners may be less affected - some specialists suggest the issue is more prevalent in North American climates and less of a concern in the UK.
items.repairVsReplace: The valley plate leak is a repairable gasket failure, not a catastrophic engine‑killer - it will not leave you stranded, and the repair involves replacing the sealant/gasket under the intake manifold. However, it is labour‑intensive (intake manifold removal) and should be addressed when the coolant level starts dropping noticeably.

items.title: Moderate oil consumption / piston ring carbonisation
items.whatHappens: Owners report moderate oil consumption of up to 0.5 litres per 1,000 km under aggressive driving. The primary cause is carbon build‑up on the piston rings, which can cause the rings to stick and fail to seal properly against the cylinder walls. The 2UR‑GSE's D‑4S fuel system (both direct and port injection) helps mitigate the carbon build‑up that plagues direct‑injection‑only engines, but it does not eliminate it entirely.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, decarbonisation treatments (chemical or media blasting) can restore ring function. If ignored, excessive oil consumption can lead to catalyst damage and, in extreme cases, bore scoring - at which point a full rebuild or replacement becomes the only option.

items.title: High‑pressure fuel pump recall - 2016-2018 GS F and RC F
items.whatHappens: Toyota issued a recall for certain 2016-2018 Lexus GS F and RC F models equipped with the 2UR‑GSE. Under specific operating conditions, one of the two high‑pressure fuel pumps can develop a fatigue crack in the fuel pump cover, potentially causing a fuel leak. Dealers replace the high‑pressure fuel pumps free of charge under the recall.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a free manufacturer recall repair - do not pay for this work out of pocket. Check with your Lexus dealer to confirm if your vehicle is affected.

items.title: Timing chain tensioner wear (rare)
items.whatHappens: There are isolated reports of timing chain tensioner wear at higher mileage. A skipped timing chain tooth can cause valve timing issues and misfires. However, this is not a common failure on the 2UR‑GSE compared to many European V8s - the engine's timing chain system is robust and long‑lived.
items.repairVsReplace: Tensioner and guide replacement is a significant job requiring front cover removal. If caught before chain failure causes valve/piston contact, repair is viable. Timing chain failure on this engine is extremely rare in normal use.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 2UR-GSE
variants.intro: The 2UR‑GSE is a single engine code with multiple output tunes across different F‑performance models. Unlike European engines with dozens of sub‑codes, the 2UR‑GSE uses a consistent internal architecture with ECU calibration differences between models. Where to find your engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped plate on the front or side of the V8 - On your V5C registration document - engine number section - Via Lexus VIN lookup - your dealer can confirm from the chassis number Power output by model (all 2UR-GSE): | Model | Power | Torque | Notes | |-------|-------|--------|-------| | Lexus IS F (2007-2014) | 416 hp (423 PS) | 505 Nm | 11.8:1 compression ratio | | Lexus RC F (2014-present) | 457-464 hp | 520 Nm | 12.3:1 compression ratio | | Lexus GS F (2015-2020) | 467-471 hp | 527 Nm | 12.3:1 compression ratio | | Lexus LC 500 (2016-present) | 464-477 hp | 520-540 Nm | Highest output variant | | Lexus IS 500 (2021-present) | 472 hp | 535 Nm | Latest F‑Sport tune | Key technical differences: - Compression ratio: Early IS F units use 11.8:1; later RC F/GS F/LC 500 units use 12.3:1 - Redline: Varies from 6,800 rpm (IS F) to 7,300 rpm (LC 500) - Fuel system: D‑4S combined direct and port injection across all variants Interchange note: Not all 2UR-GSE units are directly interchangeable - oil pan, engine mounts, ECU calibration, and ancillary fitment differ between models. An LC 500 engine has a different oil pan and mounting arrangement than an IS F unit. Always confirm the exact donor vehicle match before purchasing a replacement unit . What about the 2UR-FSE? The 2UR‑FSE is a different engine - a detuned hybrid variant used in the LS 600h and Toyota Century. It shares the same block architecture but has different internals, different compression ratio, and a hybrid drive system. A 2UR‑FSE cannot be swapped into a 2UR‑GSE application.

relatives.description: the naturally aspirated V8 that preceded the 2UR‑GSE in Lexus's larger vehicles. The 1UR‑FE was the base engine for the LS 460 and GS 460, producing lower power (380 hp) and lacking the high‑compression, high‑revving character of the 2UR‑GSE. While robust, it does not share the 2UR‑GSE's D‑4S fuel system or Yamaha‑tuned internals.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 2UR-GSE - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 2UR‑GSE **can make sense** for this engine specifically because of its legendary reliability - many units exceed 150,000 miles without major issues. However, you must verify: (1) whether the valley plate leak has been addressed, (2) oil consumption history, and (3) whether any recalls (fuel pump) have been completed. Used units from LC 500s (lower‑stress GT use) may be preferable to those from IS Fs (often tracked/hard‑driven) . The average used 2UR‑GSE costs around **£5,280** in the UK . Learn more about used engines .

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned 2UR‑GSE is the **safest bet for a long‑term replacement** - the rebuild should address the valley plate leak (new sealant/gasket), inspect and decarbonise the piston rings, replace timing chain tensioners and guides, and rebuild the high‑pressure fuel pumps. Given the known failure modes (valley plate, oil consumption), a recon unit with documented valley plate work and ring inspection is worth the premium over a used engine. Learn more about reconditioned engines .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for high‑value hosts (LC 500, RC F, IS 500) where the vehicle value exceeds £25,000-£60,000. The rebuild should include: **crankshaft inspection, new bearings, new piston rings (with decarbonisation), new timing chain and tensioners, valley plate seal replacement, and full fuel system overhaul**. Given the limited aftermarket support for this engine, choose a specialist with 2UR‑GSE experience. Learn more about rebuilt engines .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** Replacing a 2UR‑GSE through our network connects you with Lexus‑specialist workshops who understand the specific requirements of this engine, including the valley plate repair procedure and proper D‑4S fuel system handling. Learn more about supply and fit . --- **VEHICLE VALUE NOTE - mandatory read before committing:** The 2UR‑GSE sits in **high‑value performance hosts** - IS F (£12,000-£25,000 used), RC F (£20,000-£40,000), GS F (£18,000-£35,000), LC 500 (£35,000-£65,000+), and IS 500 (£40,000-£60,000) . Replacement costs of £6,500-£14,000 represent **15-40% of vehicle value** on most examples, making replacement financially viable for all but the oldest, highest‑mileage IS F examples. **However:** If your 2UR‑GSE is affected by the **fuel pump recall**, that work is **free** - do not pay for it. If your vehicle is approaching the replacement cost threshold (sub‑£12,000 IS Fs with high mileage), evaluate scrap/part‑exchange value carefully before committing to a £6,500+ replacement.

the 2UR‑GSE remains in current production for the LC 500 and IS 500 F‑Sport, making it Lexus's flagship naturally aspirated V8. The future of the 2UR‑GSE is uncertain as Lexus transitions to hybrid and electric powertrains.

items.question: Should I buy a used 2UR-GSE engine or go for a reconditioned unit?
items.answer: A used 2UR-GSE can be a sensible option because of the engine's legendary reliability - many units exceed 150,000 miles with only minor issues. However, you must verify: (1) whether the valley plate leak has been addressed, (2) oil consumption history, and (3) whether the fuel pump recall has been completed. Used: only consider with full provenance and documented service history. Reconditioned: the safest option with a 12-24 month warranty and known issues addressed. Rebuilt: best for high-value hosts (LC 500, RC F) where the vehicle is worth keeping long-term.

items.question: How do I identify if my engine is the 2UR-GSE and not the 2UR-FSE?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the engine block (usually on the front or side of the V8) and appears on your V5C registration document. The 2UR-GSE is the high-performance naturally aspirated version used in F-models, while the 2UR-FSE is the hybrid version used in the LS 600h and Toyota Century. The 2UR-GSE has 'GSE' stamped on the block; the 2UR-FSE has 'FSE'. The 2UR-FSE has a different compression ratio (11.8:1 vs 12.3:1 on later GSE units). The 2UR-FSE is mated to a hybrid system - if your vehicle is a non-hybrid F-model, it has the 2UR-GSE. Check your V5C under 'Engine number' - the code is the first part.
